A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SELFORG work. The text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across appendix reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracies, heterogeneous-agent experiments, token measurements and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original correctness-correlation, dynamic-role, aggregation, memory/tool and coding evaluations.

M1.justification: The core contribution estimation, graph construction, default aggregation and early-stopping procedures are retained. v2 adds experimental adaptations with dynamic roles (D.5), persistent agent scratchpads and Python arithmetic checks (F.4), extending agent behavior without replacing the orchestration algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds actual coding evaluations on HumanEval and SRDD with Qwen-1.5B. This substantially extends empirical task coverage beyond v1's mathematical, scientific and knowledge reasoning benchmarks, which are retained.

E2.justification: Self-Consistency becomes an evaluated comparator in Tables 9 and 10. Table 8 adds comparisons against uniform-centroid aggregation, two majority-voting variants and highest-contributor selection. Comparator membership in the retained main experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added experiments substantially expand evaluation design: D.3 samples seven queries per benchmark, F.3 controls the aggregation rule, and D.5/F.4 introduce dynamic-role and memory/tool conditions. Appendix G introduces execution-based HumanEval pass@1 and SRDD completeness/executability/consistency scoring. These are additional protocols; the original reasoning settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 expands the single illustrative correctness analysis into checks across three benchmarks (D.3), tests sensitivity to dynamic roles (D.5), reports why sessions terminate (E.1), and adds aggregation and memory/tool ablations (F.3–F.4). The earlier embedding, agent-count and graph-reformation analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 adds mean-and-standard-deviation reporting for aggregation results in Table 8, explicitly over three runs, and coding results in Table 10, whose run count is unspecified. The original benchmark tables retain point estimates; v1 already reported 100 generations for its illustrative correctness analysis.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation scores are retained, while substantial new results are reported. Table 10 gives SELFORG 48.97 ± 0.89 on HumanEval and 60.13 ± 0.90 on SRDD. Table 9 adds memory-plus-tools scores of 40.0/54.2 on GSM-Hard/MATH versus base scores of 38.0/52.4. Additional results cover aggregation, correctness probabilities, dynamic roles and stopping frequencies.

T1.justification: The theorem, corollaries, lemmas, formal assumptions and Appendix A proof arguments retain their substance. Small notation/indexing edits do not introduce a substantive theoretical revision. D.3 supplies empirical checks of the existing motivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about response-conditioned orchestration, Shapley-inspired contribution estimation and correctness amplification across weak and strong backbones. The appendix additions do not redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: D.3 newly identifies near-chance behavior as a condition where a dominant correct-answer cluster is not expected. F.3 attributes naive voting failures to option-letter parsing, while D.5 and F.4 add interpretations concerning independence from fixed roles and compatibility with memory/tools.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly supplies an implementation repository URL. F.4 specifies memory as a scratchpad persisted across rounds and the tool as a sandboxed Python REPL for arithmetic checks. Previously documented prompts, embeddings, thresholds and round settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds AgentNet and MorphAgent to the discussion of decentralized coordination, plus references supporting HumanEval and Self-Consistency. The central positioning against fixed or query-conditioned topologies, external judges and trained graph generators is retained.

P1.justification: Existing prose receives limited copyediting, the publication header changes and an acknowledgment is added. Efficient SELFORG moves from D.3 to Appendix E, and the ablation appendix becomes F. The main narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The appendix gains a substantial set of displays: similarity heatmaps and dynamic-role ranks (Figures 8 and 10), plus tables for correctness probabilities, termination, aggregation, memory/tools and coding (Tables 5–6 and 8–10). Existing displays are retained with some relocation and renumbering; Figure 1 changes its embedding labels.

improvement.justification: The added aggregation controls, broader correctness checks, coding evaluations and selective uncertainty reporting provide useful support beyond v1, while the repository link improves reproducibility information. These gains remain limited by incomplete reporting for new experiments, including Table 10's unspecified run count. D.3 also treats a probability comparison as supporting Lemma 2 without establishing its geometric assumptions, so the additional evidence does not resolve the theoretical support gap.
